title: Conservative Oxygen for Unresponsive Patients after Cardiac Arrest
shortTitle: LOGICAL: conservative oxygen did not improve functional survival
authors: LOGICAL Investigators and the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Clinical Trials Group
summary: This trial enrolled 1,840 ventilated adults who remained unresponsive after cardiac arrest. Conservative oxygen did not improve favorable functional survival at 180 days compared with a liberal strategy.
whyItMatters: The studied restrictive oxygen protocol did not improve long-term recovery. Do not extrapolate the result to initial resuscitation before oxygenation can be measured reliably.
limitations: ICU population rather than active arrest; primary outcomes were available for fewer patients than enrolled. The confidence interval does not establish equivalence.
population: Unresponsive ventilated adults after cardiac arrest in 53 ICUs.
intervention: SpO2 lower limit 90%, upper alarm 95%, permitting FiO2 reduction to 0.21.
comparator: Same lower SpO2 limit, no upper saturation limit, minimum FiO2 0.30.
primaryEndpoint: Survival with GOS-E at least 5 at 180 days.
findings: Favorable functional survival: 38.2% versus 39.7%; RR 0.97 (95% CI 0.87-1.09).
No adverse events were reported in the abstract.
evidenceNotes: Abstract reviewed; full text unavailable. Complete indexed PubMed abstract reviewed; June 10 first-online date independently confirmed on publisher page. August print date was excluded.
